$source: ~/JHD/captures/examples/example-templates-inventory-2026-07-28.md (DS Examples page, JHD-Spec-DesignSystem, desktop MCP read 2026-07-28). Operator ruling recorded there: the Example frames ARE the page templates.
$conventions: Each block's `role` is looked up in the live DOM via [data-kind="<role>"] (the codebase's own component-root convention). A height/y/x/width field valued the literal string "content" is content-driven (depends on real project count/copy/media) and is always skipped, never a defect — see template-check.mjs's header comment.

gridChecks only apply to Desktop (D) templates: the site's own CSS gates the 12-col grid behind the `lg` breakpoint (`lg:grid-cols-12` / `.layout-grid-grid[data-columns]`); Mobile (M) layouts are single-column, so a grid-snap check there would be meaningless.
A field simply omitted (not present on the block) is not checked at all — used where the DS inventory gave no number to check against, to avoid asserting a value that was never actually sourced.

D-Home.$note: Inventory's 'hidden PaginationPage 648 at end' is a hidden Figma variant, not part of the visible Home template — intentionally not asserted (asserting it would fabricate a defect for a component that isn't supposed to render here).

styleProbes.$note: Home's NavigationHeader is explicitly annotated '(overlay)' in the inventory — floats over the hero, so its own background must stay transparent.

M-Projects.$note: The inventory doc has no dedicated M-Projects section (only D-Projects was captured) — kept minimal to what's actually sourced (the shared mobile nav chrome) rather than inventing grid/hero numbers.

D-Project.$note: header-media is the operator's known open item (HeaderMedia +48) pending the portfolio round; this spec asserts the DS Example's actual 1549 so the defect surfaces rather than being papered over. feature-text-block's 464 in the inventory is that ONE example's own prose length, not a fixed contract — feature-text.tsx (verified against source) has no height/min-height constraint, its total height is SpacerTop(space-500) + prose (unbounded) + SpacerBottom(space-600), so it's marked content-driven here rather than asserting a number the component was never built to hold to.

M-Project.$note: feature-text-block is content-driven (see D-Project's note — verified against feature-text.tsx source, no height constraint on the component).
